subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT Gateway shutdown abort active runs and their managed exec child processes, or preserve background/yielded exec sessions unless an explicit restart or kill path is used?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve active/background work on normal shutdown, so changing this is an operator-safety and product policy choice rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for any preserved background process class.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal shutdown from aborting active/background exec work and treat this as a diagnostics or documentation gap rather than a runtime cancellation change.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the session-wide exec-control contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines the reusable process ownership model.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for any preserved background process class.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history on service-managed child hardening, exec abort behavior, and the run-loop watchdog split.
